spec: Convert a numeric exam score (0-100) to a letter grade: A is 90 and above, B is 80s, C is 70s, D is 60s, otherwise F. Scores can have decimals.

inputs.note: Integer zero with floor rounding, edge case for boundary behavior.

questions.text: Should an unrecognised rounding method (e.g., "Hello World") cause an error or be ignored?
questions.why: The current code silently treats any non‑matching rounding string as "no rounding", so invalid values never raise an exception.

options.label: Invalid rounding strings are ignored and no rounding is applied.
Invalid rounding strings raise a ValueError.

questions.text: Should scores outside the 0‑100 range be rejected or clamped instead of graded normally?
questions.why: The implementation accepts negative scores (and would accept >100) and grades them using the same thresholds, returning "F" for negatives.

options.label: Out‑of‑range scores are accepted and graded like any other number.
Out‑of‑range scores raise a ValueError (or are clamped to 0‑100).

questions.text: When rounding="round", should .5 values round to the nearest even integer (banker's rounding) or always round up?
questions.why: The code uses Python's built‑in round(), which implements bankers rounding (ties to even), affecting borderline scores such as 88.5.

options.label: "round" uses Python's bankers rounding (ties to even).

resolution.clarified_spec: Convert a numeric exam score (0-100) to a letter grade: A is 90 and above, B is 80s, C is 70s, D is 60s, otherwise F. Scores can have decimals. Invalid rounding strings are ignored and no rounding is applied. Out-of-range scores are accepted and graded like any other number. The “round” method uses Python’s banker’s rounding (ties to even). Examples: 2.5, “Hello World” → F; -3.5 → F.
